title: 1 in 13 Steam games finds an audience. Will yours?
author: ilrein91
selftext:
Inspired by the question of, can AI create an original idea? Well, sort of: we can map all existing ideas (in this case: steam games) on a vector space, using descriptions, metadata, and tags. Then we can explore games naturally clustered by genre, and look at the areas where there are gaps. By selecting a new point in a gap, we can translate that embedding into game concept.

Truly original? That's up for debate. But we can mathematically ascertain the distance of nearest neighbours, and we can even look for ones that did well (over 1k reviews). At very least, it can help answer the question: what game *should* I make?

Link here: [https://spriteloom.app/](https://spriteloom.app/)

comments.author: 907Renegade
comments.body: Mine already found its place with my friends, so ive already won.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
My dream - and it seems so attainable, which is a nice plus - is that my game, should it ever be finished and released, will be played by a handful of people and bring them joy. They will remember it, even if just briefly, as something that was fun and engaging and elevated their life in that moment by a fraction of a millimetre 

The game will then fade away into the background landscape of interesting games people have made over time that aren't much remembered anymore, but perhaps occasionally stumbled across. 'Oh wow, look at this cool thing, never heard of it before, that was fun.' 

  
I do not want an 'audience'. That is a nightmare to me; the type of externality Toby Fox has written about extensively. 

And thankfully, that is unlikely to happen.
